rounds.text: The most compelling evidence for a turnaround is the aggressive accumulation of equity by promoters, who have increased their stake from 52.80% to 73.08% in under three years [E22]. This massive vote of confidence aligns with a significant acceleration in profitability, evidenced by a 65% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E10] and a 233% year-over-year surge in net profit [E32]. While the market remains cautious, the stock’s 400% growth over the last three years suggests that investors are beginning to price in this fundamental shift [E13]. The company is currently demonstrating a clear pattern of improving results, with both sales and profits growing on a quarter-over-quarter basis [E34, E35]. Conceded: the company faces severe headwinds including a 77% decline in five-year sales growth [E5], negative operating cash flow [E18], and high debtor days [E30]. Despite these historical challenges, the current trajectory of profit growth [E33] and the strong insider commitment [E22] indicate that the business is undergoing a meaningful transformation that current sentiment may be failing to fully appreciate [E36].

Aurique Ltd presents a precarious financial profile defined by a catastrophic collapse in top-line performance, with compounded sales growth plummeting by 77% over five years, 89% over three years, and 84% over the trailing twelve months [E5, E6, E7, E28]. This fundamental decay is compounded by severe operational inefficiencies, evidenced by a nine-year downward trend in operating margins and a staggering -2840% operating margin recorded in March 2018 [E14, E15]. The company’s liquidity is equally concerning, as it reported negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -3.76 Cr and Rs -2.94 Cr respectively, while simultaneously increasing its debt burden to Rs 28.68 Cr [E18, E19, E20]. Furthermore, the business faces significant solvency and operational risks, highlighted by a low interest coverage ratio, massive contingent liabilities of Rs 18.1 Cr, and an alarming debtor collection period of 1,862 days [E27, E29, E30]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated recent profit growth of 65% over the trailing twelve months and a significant increase in promoter shareholding to 73.08% [E10, E22]. Despite these recent metrics, the stock’s current valuation at 100% of its 52-week range appears disconnected from its long-term structural decline in sales and negative book value of ₹ -5.60 [E1, E4, E25].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is -77% [E5], and operating cash flow was Rs -3.76 Cr in Mar 2018 [E18]. However, the bear's focus on historical top-line decline misses the accelerating profitability turnaround that is actively driving the business, evidenced by compounded profit growth accelerating to 23% over 3 years and 65% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10]. Conceded: operating margins show a long-term downward trend [E15]. Yet, the rules-based screen explicitly highlights strong positive momentum with net profit up 233% YoY and accelerating results scoring an impressive 84/100, proving that stale sentiment is blinding observers to a live operational recovery [E32, E36]. Furthermore, promoters have heavily increased their skin in the game by 20.28 percentage points to reach 73.08% stake as of Sep 2026, demonstrating absolute insider conviction in the turnaround that dwarfs historical debt or debtor figures [E22]. Conceded: borrowings stand at Rs 28.68 Cr [E20] and debtors are high [E30]. Nevertheless, market confidence is fully justified by the company sitting 100% of the way up its 52-week range alongside robust recent quarterly profit and sales growth [E4, E34, E35].

Conceded: compounded profit growth reads 23% over 3 years and 65% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10], alongside quarterly profit and sales increases [E34, E35] and a results score of 84/100 [E36]. However, this profitability turnaround sits on a collapsing top-line foundation, proven by a 5-year compounded sales contraction of -77% and a trailing twelve-month sales drop of -84% [E5, E7]. The bull points to insider accumulation reaching 73.08% [E22], but this heavy conviction must be weighed against severe balance sheet distress, including a negative book value yielding a price-to-book ratio of -17.64x [E1], rising borrowings of Rs 28.68 Cr [E20], and an explicit flag for a low interest coverage ratio [E27]. Furthermore, the claim that market confidence justifies the stock sitting 100% up its 52-week range [E4] ignores the dangerous operational reality of 1,862-day debtors [E30], Rs 18.1 Cr in contingent liabilities [E29], and a disastrous historical operating margin of -2840% forming a multi-year downward trend [E14, E15].
